query: For high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation? Specify what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, the expected observations relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings is governed by the formation of a stable, coherent interface between the individual layers, which suppresses dislocation glide and grain boundary sliding.
generation.material_initial_state: as-deposited or annealed high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings
generation.intervention: in situ TEM or SEM characterization under elevated temperature (500°C) and constant stress (500 MPa)
generation.mechanism: suppression of dislocation glide and grain boundary sliding
generation.predicted_outcome: a 30% reduction in creep strain relative to a baseline of single-layer high-entropy alloy coatings
generation.boundary: elevated temperature (500°C) and constant stress (500 MPa)
generation.uncertainty: the exact role of individual layer composition and thickness on the coherent interface formation and stability

falsification_experiment.design: in situ TEM or SEM characterization of high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings under elevated temperature and constant stress
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the creep strain of the multilayer coatings is not reduced by at least 20% relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
